Recommended certification pathway

Why Seattle needs certified NDT personnel

Seattle sits on aerospace manufacturing and its supply chain, shipbuilding and marine repair, and refining north of the metro area. That industrial base is what creates sustained demand for qualified inspection personnel here: the assets in question — aircraft structures and composite assemblies, marine structures, refinery equipment and pressure vessels — are examined on intervals set by code rather than by preference, and the examinations have to be performed and interpreted by people whose qualification can be evidenced.

In practice that means the methods pulled hardest in this market are penetrant and eddy current on aerospace parts, ultrasonic including composite techniques, radiography. A qualification programme built for Seattle should follow that demand rather than cover every method thinly.

Which level you need for Seattle work

Level I performs specific calibrations and examinations and records results under direction. It is where most people entering Seattle inspection work start, and for aircraft structures and composite assemblies it is usually reached in a single method first rather than several at once.

Level II sets up and calibrates equipment, interprets and evaluates results against the applicable code, and writes the report. This is the level most contracts in Washington actually specify, because it is the level that can make an accept-or-reject call without supervision.

Level III establishes techniques and procedures, approves them, interprets codes and specifications, and takes responsibility for the qualification and examination of Level I and II personnel. It is also the level that signs the Written Practice an auditor will ask for. For operators running penetrant and eddy current on aerospace parts across multiple sites, Level III capability is the difference between owning your inspection programme and renting it.

How training reaches Seattle

Atlantis does not operate a classroom in Seattle, and it is worth being straightforward about that rather than implying otherwise. Training is delivered on-site at your own facility anywhere in Washington and the surrounding region — which for a corporate buyer is usually the better arrangement anyway, since the practical specimens can reflect the aircraft structures and composite assemblies your people will actually be examining, and nobody loses days to travel.

Where you have only one or two candidates, the practical alternatives are a scheduled cohort at one of our locations, or blended delivery with theory completed online and supervised practical arranged locally. Which of the three is right depends on headcount and on how quickly you need people qualified; tell us both and we will say plainly which we would recommend.

Certification route: ASNT, ISO 9712, and which your employer needs

Two models operate in the United States and they are not interchangeable. Under SNT-TC-1A, certification is granted by the employer against the employer's own Written Practice — flexible, and the reason auditors ask to see that document rather than a certificate. ISO 9712 and schemes such as PCN and CSWIP certify through an independent body, so the certificate is portable between employers. ANSI/ASNT CP-189 sits between them as a standard rather than a recommended practice.

Which you need is a contractual question, not a technical one. Plenty of Washington contracts name one specifically, and candidates who choose the wrong route lose months. If you are unsure which your client base expects, that is worth a five-minute conversation before you enrol anyone.

Frequently asked questions

Is there NDT training near me in Seattle?

Atlantis delivers training on-site at facilities across Washington rather than from a fixed classroom in Seattle. For a team, that is normally faster and cheaper than sending people away; for an individual, a scheduled cohort or blended delivery is usually the better route. Tell us which you are and we will point you at the honest option, including if that is someone else.

How long does it take to qualify at Level II?

It depends on the method and on how much documented experience you already hold, because the requirement is training hours and experience hours, not training alone. Someone already working under supervision in the method progresses considerably faster than someone starting cold. We will map your existing hours against the requirement before you commit to anything.

Can our own staff be certified without an outside body?

Under SNT-TC-1A, yes — that is precisely the model, and it requires a compliant Written Practice and a qualified Level III to administer it. Many operators use an outsourced Level III for exactly this. If you do not currently have one, that is the gap to close first, because without it the certifications you issue will not survive an audit.

Do you train all methods?

UT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus advanced techniques including phased array and TOFD, and preparation for API 510, 570 and 653 inspector certification. For a Seattle programme we would normally suggest starting with penetrant and eddy current on aerospace parts and adding from there as the work demands.
